Commentary.Commentary: Full marks to the Islanders for showing discipline with both bat and ball. 28 overs left in the day. Enough time to wrap the match up? Join us back at 2.20 pm local (0850 GMT) for the final session.

Afghanistan will feel disappointed. With plenty of spinners in their ranks, they were way below par as compared to Rahkeem Cornwall. Amir Hamza did pick up 5 wickets but there was no consistent control over the lines or lengths from both, Hamza and Rashid. If the skipper had bowled to his true potential, perhaps this could have become a one-inning shootout.

90 is the lead for West Indies then. That is a massive positive, given the turn the pitch has taken so far. Brooks' Nelson has enabled the Caribbeans to be in a strong position, with good support from Campbell and Dowrich. TEA HAS BEEN TAKEN AS WELL, given that 10 minutes are left for the break.

OUT! LBW! Five-wicket haul for Hamza on debut. Flighted delivery on middle, Roach looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw and the umpire raises his finger. WEST INDIES ARE ALL OUT FOR 277!
Short delivery on off, Warrican makes room and cuts it towards point. The batsmen cross ends.
Flighted delivery on off, Warrican defends it off the front foot.
Cut copy paste, the action from the last ball. Pitches on off, Roach comes forward to defend. The ball turns away to beat the outside edge once again.
Beaten! Another beauty. Roach can't do much about this one. It pitches on off and once again goes away. Roach looks to get behind the line of the ball to defend but gets beaten.
Quicker one and on middle, Warrican nudges it behind square leg for a single.
On the pads, Roach tucks it towards fine leg for a single.

Huge appeal for caught behind. Turn and bounce there. It pitches on off and turns away as Roach comes forward to defend. The ball turns away to beat the outside edge and the Afghans appeal but not out says the umpire.
Full and on the pads, tucked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully pressed out.
Tossed up outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
A short ball now, punched back to the bowler once more.
Around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Landed outside off, spinning away, Warrican lunges to defend but misses.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
The batsman has nudged the ball fine down the leg side. They manage to come back for the second.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads. The fielding side is asking the question. The umpire shows no interest in the appeal.
The batsman fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad.
Floated delivery on middle, Roach defends it out.
Flighted delivery on off, Roach looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire shakes his head.
The second new ball is available now. But it is not being taken right now.
Fuller and around off, pushed towards cover.
Jomel Warrican is the last man in.

OUT! Bowled' em! The centurion departs now, in search of quick runs. A fullish length ball on middle, Brooks lines himself for the slog sweep but plays the shot all around the ball. It goes behind and shatters the wood work behind. Hamza has 4 and the dropped chance does not cost much to the Afghans. End of an excellent innings.
Full and on off, pushed towards gully.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Dropped! A tough chance this one. Slightly shortish length ball, too close to cut Brooks goes for it. He manages a thick outside edge which flies right of the first slip fielder off the gloves of the keeper. It goes towards third man for a couple of runs. How costly will this chance be?
On middle, pushed back the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Around off, well pushed out.
Full on middle, whipped through mid-wicket for a brace.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Short and outside off, cut through point for a boundary!
On off, defended from within the crease.

Appeal for LBW! The umpire is unmoved. Hamza tosses one up and on off, Roach goes for the defensive push but the ball spins past his defensive shot and struck him on the pads. The Afghan players go up in appeal but the umpire thinks otherwise.
Full and around middle, Brooks defends it to mid on and takes a quick single.
Outside off, Brooks taps it to the off side.
BEATEN! Tossed up around off, Brooks looks to defend off the front foot. The ball goes past the outside edge and into the mitts of the keeper.
Tossed up around off, Brooks blocks it back to the bowler.
Fuller and on off, Roach this time keeps it out.
Another LBW appeal but this time the umpire turns it down. It pitches around off this time. Roach comes forward to defense but is hit on the pads. An appeal follows but not out says the umpire.
Kemar Roach walks in at no. 10.

OUT! LBW! Skipper strikes and the big man has to depart. A boundary and now he has to go. Got 7 wickets with the ball but cannot contribute much with the willow. Superb comeback from Rashid. This pitched outside off and then turned into Cornwall. Rahkeem looked to defend but missed. The ball hits the pads and Rashid roars out an appeal. The umpire raises the finger. Cornwall doesn't seem to be happy. Seems like he nicked the ball there. Yes, the replays confirm and the big man was clearly not happy as he was trudging off, showing his bat to the umpire there. A wicket for the Afghans nonetheless.
FOUR! Up and over! Full and outside off, Cornwall gets underneath it and biffs it over cover! The fielder gives it a chase but comes second best, even with a slide.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

MAIDEN TEST TON FOR SHAMARH BROOKS! It seems like an age to cover his travels from 75 to 100 but he has got there. His first century in Tests, coming in at a time when his side needed it from him. Gets there with a punch through covers. A bit of yes-yes and a no-no but eventually, they get the single. 7th West Indian batsman to register their maiden Test ton on Indian soil. 69 balls it has taken him post Lunch to get to the landmark.
On middle and off, punched down towards mid on again. Still on 99...
Around off, punched towards mid on.
Around off, punched down to the bowler.
Full and around middle, watchfully defended.
Around middle, punched towards mid on for a single.
Flatter one around off, Brooks cuts it through point. The fielder in the deep runs across to his left and saves a run. In the meantime the batsmen cross for a couple.

Beauty from Rashid. Very rarely have we seen him bowl good stuff today. This one pitched on off and spins away. Brooks looks to defend this towards the off side but the ball further spins away to go past the outside edge.
Brooks is happy to stay on the back foot and punch this tossed up delivery to the off side.
Flatter and outside off, Brooks looks to cut but gets an bottom edge on it as the ball goes to the off side.
Full and on off, Brooks drives it through covers and gets a comfortable two.
Flatter outside off, Brooks slaps it to covers.
Tossed up, Cornwall defends it to the off side.
On off, defended to the off side.
Flatter and around off, Cornwall goes for the cut but fails to get bat on ball.
Flighted and around off, Cornwall pushes it to the off side.
Full and on leg, Brooks works it to the leg side for a run.
Tossed up outside off, Brooks defends inside the line.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
Landed outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Into the 90s now! Fractionally short and that is enough for Brooks. He rocks back and pulls it with venom to the mid-wicket fence.
Full and around off, well blocked out.
Outside off, left alone.
A beauty to start! Landed outside off, Brooks looks to defend but the ball spins a mile after pitching. Brooks looks to defend but then aims to take the bat away. Is late and gets beaten.
Rashid Khan comes on to bowl again. 26-5-88-2 so far.
BEATEN! Flatter and outside off, Cornwall goes for the cut but fails to lay bat on ball.
The giant Cornwall defends the ball to the off side off the back foot.
Rahkeem Cornwall is the new batsman in.

OUT! That is a terrific piece of stumping from Afsar Zazai! For all his shouts and constant chatter behind the wickets, this is some excellent work because his concentration is not wavering at all. The tall Holder fails to hold himself and is gone cheaply. Hamza tosses one up around off and gives it a bit off more air to it. Holder lunges to defend but is beaten by pace. His back leg goes up in the air slightly, probably for not even half a second. But that is enough for Zazai behind the wickets as he is super quick to whip the bails off in a flash. He is confident and goes for the appeal. The umpire goes upstairs to check and then the replays come in. It shows that Jason had lifted his foot in the air and got back in, but only after Afsar had dislodged the bails. Holder takes the long walk back.

Stumping appeal taken upstairs against Jason Holder! The keeper seems pretty confident. Here come the replays. Holder's back leg seems to be in the air. The bails are off in a flash. Out it will be! Superb work from Afsar Zazai.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and on off, defended to point.
Tossed up around off, played to mid off for a quick single.
FOUR! This is good batting from Jason Holder. Flighted delivery outside off, Holder drives it through covers for a boundary.
Loopy delivery on off, Brooks punches it towards point. The batsmen take a run. THE LEAD NOW TOUCHES 50.
BEATEN! Tossed up delivery outside off, Brooks looks to defend but misses it.
Floated delivery on off, Holder flicks it towards mid-wicket and takes a run.
Tossed up delivery on off, Holder drives it through covers. The batsmen pick up a couple. The lead moves to 49.
Flighted delivery on middle, Holder flicks it towards mid-wicket.

DRINKS BREAK! It has been a solid hour for the West Indies where they have lost the only wicket of Shane Dowrich. On the other hand, Afghanistan have toiled hard and need quick wickets to put the pressure back on West Indies.
Brooks defends this flighted ball to the off side.
Loopy on off, Brooks taps it to the off side.
Tossed up up on leg, Brooks goes for the flick but fails to lay bat on ball.
On off, defended right under his eyes by Brooks.
Flighted delivery on off, Brooks defends it to the off side.
Tossed up on off, defended to covers.

Flighted delivery on middle, Holder looks to defend but misses it and gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire shakes his head. It was spinning too much and could have missed the leg stump.
Floated delivery on off, Brooks plays it towards point. The batsmen take a run.
FOUR! Lovely shot. Tossed up delivery on off, Brooks hammers it straight back. Zahir leaps to take the catch but the ball is well over his head. Down the ground goes the ball to the fence.
Flighted delivery on off, Brooks defends it out.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Brooks blocks it well.
Floated delivery on middle, Brooks keeps it out.
FOUR! Good shot. Flighted delivery on middle, Holder lofts it straight back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Loopy delivery on middle, Holder looks to defend but gets an inside edge. It goes to short fine leg.
Floated delivery on off, Holder plays it to point.
Flighted delivery on off, Brooks drives it towards mid off. The fielder goes for a direct hit at the bowler's end but misses it. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Brooks drives it to mid on.
Floated delivery on middle, Brooks defends it off the front foot.

Umpire Nitin Menon has a chat with Afsar Zazai. One feels that the complaint is about excessive appealing and it is pretty much natural that anyone will feel annoyed. Asghar Afghan now has a chat with umpire Paul Reiffel and he too, seems to be telling the same point.
Bowls a googly on middle, Holder looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes towards first slip where it falls short of the fielder.
Tossed up delivery on leg, Holder looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire shakes his head.
Flighted delivery on off, Brooks defends it off the front foot.
Jason Holder walks in now, at number 8, replacing Dowrich.

OUT! LBW! Zahir Khan gets the breakthrough at last. After numerous cries of LBW and caught behinds, finally, the umpire has consented to one. End of an excellent partnership between Shane Dowrich and Shamarh Brooks. Flighted delivery on middle, Dowrich looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw and the umpire raises his finger. This one looked plumb, with the ball showing to be pitching in line and just spinning in a bit, hitting the batsman in front of middle stump. A very good knock from Dowrich. Came in at a time when West Indies were in a bit of a bother and has given some ascendancy to his team now. West Indies now lead by 37.
Full delivery on off, Dowrich drives it to mid off.
Flighted delivery on off, Brooks defends it off the front foot.
Zahir Khan is back on as well. 10-1-40-1 so far.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Shamarh defends it off the back foot.
Loopy delivery on middle, Brooks keeps it out.
Floated delivery on middle, Brooks blocks it off the front foot.

Analyzing Shamarh Brooks, he comes across as one of those few unusual West Indian batsmen who have a very good technique. Less of flair. He has played the spinners very tactfully. While attacking, he has looked to go in front of square. On the other hand, he has turned the strike over by targetting the areas behind square.
Bowls it down the leg side, Brooks looks to go after it but misses it.
Flighted delivery on off, Brooks defends it out.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Dowrich flicks it through square leg. The batsmen take a run.
Amir Hamza returns. 19-3-59-2 so far.
Outside off, Brooks shoulders arms to this one.
On a good length on middle, Brooks blocks it off the back foot.
Full delivery on middle, Dowrich flicks it through square leg. The batsmen take a run.
A sharp bouncer, around off, coming in, right at the head of the batsman and Dowrich has to get down in a hurry. Ahmadzai gives a long stare to Dowrich.
A full toss, this one swings, around middle, pushed with a straight bat towards mid on. A slight fumble, as the fielder takes his eyes off the ball seeing the batsmen take off for the single.
A length ball outside off, coming in with the angle, Brooks is right behind the line to defend.
Loopy delivery on middle, Dowrich keeps it out.
Floated delivery on middle, Dowrich defends it out. He was late in bringing his bat down. Almost gone plumb LBW.
Short delivery on middle, Brooks looks to pull but gets it off the toe end of the bat. It goes towards square leg. The batsmen take a single.
Flighted delivery on off, Brooks defends it off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Brooks defends it off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on off, Brooks defends it off the front foot.
Zahir Khan to bowl. 9-1-39-1 are his figures so far.
On a good length on off again, Shane keeps it out.
Looks like there is a bit of drift visible now. It is not exactly reverse swing but the time is ripe for the same. 63 overs done and Afghanistan might rue the lack of fast bowlers.
Good length delivery on off, Dowrich defends it out.
On a good length on middle, Dowrich flicks it to mid-wicket.
Full delivery on middle, Dowrich plays it back to the bowler.

FOUR! Magnificent timing. Everything so good about that shot. Not a bad ball at all. Around off, on a length, coming in with the angle, Dowrich just stands in his crease and shows the full face of the bat, punching it towards cover. Now, the ball is in the gap and initially it seems like it is just a single. But the lush outfield transfers pace onto the ball and it keeps running away from the fielders. Dowrich has moved to 40 now, in a stand of 70. The lead is worth 33 as well.
On a length outside off, pushed away from his body towards point.
Floated delivery on middle, Brooks defends it off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on middle, Dowrich nudges it towards square leg. The batsmen take a single.
Loopy delivery on middle, Dowrich defends it out.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Brooks looks to sweep but gets it off the pads. It goes towards fine leg. The batsmen cross ends. The umpire gives it as a leg bye.
Flighted delivery on middle, Brooks defends it off the back foot.
Floated delivery on leg, Dowrich looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. It goes towards the leg side. The batsmen cross ends. The umpire gives it as a leg bye.
Flighted delivery on middle, Brooks keeps it out.

FOUR LEG BYES! Wayward from Ahmadzai. He bowls one on a length but the line is on the leg stump, Brooks looks to flick but gets it off the pads. It goes fine down the leg side. The keeper Zazai dives to his left but the ball runs through him and into the fine leg fence.
Outside off, Brooks lets it go.
Bowls a bumper, Brooks ducks under it.
Floated delivery on middle, Dowrich looks to defend but gets an inside edge on this one. It goes towards the leg side. The batsmen take a run.
Bowls a bouncer, Dowrich does well to duck under it. Is it the first bouncer of the day? Don't remember any bouncers being bowled today.

Huge shout for LBW! This looked closer than the previous one. Or ones. Flighted delivery on off, Brooks looks to defend but misreads the googly. He is hit on the pads and Rashid belts out an appeal but umpire Reiffel shakes his head. Probably height could have been a factor.
Outside off, Brooks leaves it alone.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Brooks defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Excellent shot. Floated delivery outside off, Brooks drives it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
Flighted delivery on middle, Brooks blocks it off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery on off, Brooks plays it to covers.
Full delivery on middle, Dowrich flicks it to mid-wicket.

Dowrich gets lucky on the bottom edge. Ahamdzai bowls one on a length and outside off, Dowrich  looks to cut it through the point region but gets a bottom edge. The ball bounces near the side of the pitch and goes towards the off side.
On a good length on off, Dowrich blocks it off the back foot.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and around off, driven straight back to the bowler.
Around off, on a length, watchfully defended.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Another one on middle, which keeps low, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and down the leg side, Shane looks to sweep but misses.
Tossed up on middle, Dowrich keeps it out. Rashid has been very inconsistent, right from the morning. The lengths have not been right, nor the lines.

FOUR! That stayed low, but it was played very well. A short ball, down the leg side, Dowrich looked to pull but the cherry stayed low. However, he adjusted well, rolled his wrists and pulled it all along the ground to the fine leg fence. 50-RUN STAND IS UP AS WELL. Of those, Dowrich has scored 33.
Tossed up delivery on middle and leg, Dowrich looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire shakes his head.
Outside off, Brooks shoulders arms to this one.
Full delivery on off, Brooks drives it back towards the bowler.
On a good length on off, Brooks defends it off the back foot.
Landed outside off, Shamarh gets a big stride forward and shoulders arms.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and wide outside off, Brooks slashes hard but misses.
Yamin Ahmadzai to bowl from the other end. 5-1-17-0 are his figures so far.

FOUR! You need to have this as a norm, don't you? One bad ball in an over at least. At least. Short delivery on middle, Dowrich rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. The stand is now worth 49.
Full delivery on middle, Dowrich drives it back towards the bowler.

Massive shout for LBW! Turned down. Rashid is not happy. Floated delivery on off, Dowrich comes forward to defend but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire shakes his head. Was impact outside off? Looks so, from the replays. It was a the googly, which was not picked by the keeper batsman.
Flighted delivery on off, SD keeps it out.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Shane defends it off the back foot.
Full toss on middle, Dowrich flicks it to mid-wicket.

We are back for the second session. The Afghanistan players are out in the middle. Shamarh Brooks and Shane Dowrich will resume their innings for West Indies. Rashid Khan will start the proceedings after Lunch.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

Shamarh Brooks has played just 2 Tests but he seems to be a man brimming with confidence. His 75 from 129 balls have been a combination of attack and defense, punishing the poor balls and seeing out the good ones. Afghanistan spinners have bowled well, with plenty of shouts from behind the wickets but the counter-attack from the Caribbeans has meant that the dot balls have not been allowed to pile up. Join us back at 12.10 pm local (0640 GMT) to see how the afternoon session pans out.

Starting the day in foggy conditions, the pair of Campbell and Brooks continued from where it left off last night. The duo added 82 for the third wicket, before a cheeky shot and a blinder from Ihsanullah brought about the downfall of Campbell. That in turn, led to a collapse as West Indies slipped from 116/2 to 150/5. But since then, Dowrich has given excellent company to Brooks and the partnership is worth 45 now.

Entertaining session. 127/3 in 33 overs. West Indies have gone past Afghanistan's score and with 5 wickets left, they will be hoping to stretch this current lead of 8 and put more pressure on Rashid Khan and his team.

FOUR! A boundary to end a fruitful morning session for West Indies. Coming to the ball, it was a fuller one on middle and leg. Brooks just gets inside the line and helps it on its way towards fine leg. The ball crosses the fence for  a boundary. That will also be LUNCH ON DAY 2.
Outside off, left alone.
Length and on off, defended off the back foot.
BRAVE LEAVE! Ahmadzai brings the ball in from a good length but Brooks is well aware of his off pole as he shoulders arms to it.
Full and on middle, defended off the back foot.

FOUR! WEST INDIES TAKE THE LEAD! Length ball coming back on, Brooks brings his bat down in time and gets an edge on it. The ball races to the fine leg fence. The fielder at fine leg was very square and hence failed to cut that boundary.

Finally a pacer! The first in this session. Yamin Ahmadzai to bowl. 4-1-9-0 are his figures so far. Afghan and Rashid are involved in a long chat. Ahmadzai is still marking his runup and already a minute has ticked by. By the looks of it, Afghanistan are in no hurry to get this over started. Should be the last one before Lunch.
Goes back and blocks it out.
Around off once more, punched towards short mid-wicket.
Around off, more away spin, punched towards short extra cover.
Short and outside off, spinning away, punched straight to cover.
Landed around off, punched back to the bowler.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.

FOUR! Poor stuff from Rashid. He overpitches and Brooks just relies on the timing there as he drives it through mid on. Asghar Afghan initially looked interested but gave up. The ball races to the long on fence for a boundary.
Tossed up around off, defended to the off side.
Full and on off, Shane gets an inside edge onto his pad and past the short leg fielder for a run.
Full and around off, Shane pushes it to the off side.
Tossed up on off, pushed to short cover.

Huge shout for LBW, turned down. Impact seemed to be outside off. Full and outside off, Dowrich got a full-stride lunge to defend but missed and was hit on the pads. The ball deflected towards first slip who was not able to stop it cleanly and the ball went behind. The fielder himself had to go and retrieve it. A leg bye taken.
A touch short, punched back to the bowler.
Full and around middle, well blocked out.
Comes around the wicket now, lands it short of full outside off, Brooks punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

A short ball, around off, Dowrich looks to pull and hits it hard to the man at short leg, Ibrahim Zadran it is over there and he yelps in pain as the ball deflects off his right boot through square leg. The keeper himself runs after the ball to collect. A single taken.
On off, Brooks blocks it from within the crease.
It is a bit demoralizing for the players. There are hardly 20 spectators in the stands to watch the game. From the positive aspect, that seems to be 20 more than what we saw yesterday.

Leading edgeeeee! But safe. Dowrich looks to flick this loopy delivery on middle towards mid-wicket but closes his bat face early and gets leading edge. The ball goes towards point and the batsmen cross ends.
Brooks flicks this full one on middle towards the leg side for a run.
Tossed up on off, Brooks blocks it off the back foot.
Brave leave. Not far from the off pole. Brooks knows where his off stump is and lifts his bat at the last moment to the straighter one from Rashid.
Tossed up on off, defended off the front foot to the off side.
Rashid Khan is back on. 20-5-67-2 are his figures so far.
On off, blocked towards the off side.
Full and around off, defended to the off side.
Flighted around off, pushed to covers.
On off, driven to short cover.
Full and on middle, pushed back to the bowler off the back foot.
Full and on middle and leg, defended to short leg.
Landed outside leg, spinning further down, Brooks shoulders arms.
Full and around off, worked wide of long on for a single.
Around leg stump, turning down, flicked through fine leg for a couple. Dowrich moves to 21.
Full and outside off, driven majestically towards mid off.
Down the leg side again, Shane misses his flick this time. The ball goes off his pads through the vacant leg slip region and the batsmen return for a brace. Leg byes signalled.
A short ball, down the leg side, Dowrich pulls it comfortably through fine leg for a couple.
Flatter and outside off, Dowrich punches it off the back foot to the off side for a run.
Flighted one around off, Dowrich blocks it off the back foot.
Tossed up around off, Dowrich defends it to the offside off the front foot.
On off, defended off the back foot.

Appeal for LBW! Turned down by the umpire. Hamza tosses one up and Dowrich looks to defend. The ball beats his defensive push and crashes onto his pads. Hamza appeals straightaway but the umpire gives him a blank look. Replays later show that the ball might be doing too much down the leg side.
Full and on middle, defended to mid on.
Amir Hamza is back on. 15-1-56-2 are his figures so far.
Full and outside off, Brooks drives it through cover. The fielder there dives and saves runs.
Full and on off, defended towards point.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to mid on.
On off, driven straight to covers.
Full and outside off, slapped to covers.
Tossed up around off, pushed to mid off.
Flatter and outside off, cut straight to point.
Flighted one on off, Dowrich defends it.
Flatter on middle, Dowrich pulls it but straight to mid-wicket.
Full on the pads, Brooks flicks it to fine leg for a single.
Flighted one on middle, defended to short leg.
Full and on off, Brooks blocks it to the off side.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
Around off, the skidder, Shane looks to block from the crease but gets it off the bottom half of the bat through backward square leg for a single.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.

LBW? Caught? Neither given. Plenty of shouts and umpire Nitin Menon asks the players to calm down. Full and around off, spinning in, Dowrich looked to defend but missed and was hit on the pads. Now, the bowler appealed for LBW but the keeper was more interested in seeing the ball lob to second slip. There were cries of joy all around but the umpire was very calm. Replays do not detect any inside edge while the ball is seemingly going down the leg side.
Around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and around off, Dowrich gets a big stride forward and defends in front of his pads.
Flatter and outside off, Brooks punches the ball to the off side off the back foot.
On off, defended to the off side.

EDGED AND SAFE! Brooks is riding his luck here. A chance goes abegging  for Afghanistan. Rashid tosses one up outside off, Brooks defends it, only to get an outside edge. The ball lobs in the air. Zazai behind the wickets goes for the catch but it hits his shoulder and drops in front of him. Zazai tries to take it on the second attempt but misses.
Tossed up on middle, defended to short leg.
Full on off, pushed to mid off by Brooks.
Tossed up on off, Brooks defends it to the off side.
Flighted delivery on off, Dowrich blocks it off the back foot.
FOUR! That is put away! Full toss on off, Dowrich drives it through covers for a boundary.
Short delivery on middle, Dowrich pulls it to mid-wicket.
Bowls it down the leg side, Dowrich looks to flick but misses it.
Full delivery on off, Dowrich drives it to mid off.
Floated delivery on middle, Dowrich flicks it towards square leg. The batsmen take a single.
Flighted delivery on middle, Dowrich blocks it off the back foot.
FOUR! Poor delivery from Rashid. Short delivery on middle, Dowrich pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Outside off, the googly, Dowrich offers no shot to this one.
Landed outside off, dabbed in front of second slip.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Rippa. Landed outside off, Dowrich looks to defend but the ball grips the surface and then whizzes past the outside edge, taking an extravagant turn.
Loopy delivery on off, Dowrich looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes towards third man. The fielder chases it and does well to stop it. The batsmen get three runs.
Floated delivery on off, Dowrich keeps it out.

Right. All set to start. John Campbell will resume their overnight partnership, which is worth 34. Who will start off proceedings with the ball? Amir Hamza it will be, to bowl to Campbell first up. Here we go...

WEATHER - How is the weather? Winter is setting in India and given that Lucknow is closer to the northern parts, it is pretty chill and hazy. Visibility could be an issue but the good news is that there will not be any delay and we are set to start on time.

How do the hosts look at this? No point in dwelling over the fact that they could manage only 187. Bygones are bygones. If they can manage to restrict the West Indies lead to under 50, there is still a possibility of a one-inning shootout. Once that happens, 4th innings batting is never gonna be easy. The Caribbeans are stroke-makers, so perhaps stifle the run flow, induce mistakes and get wickets would be the mantra. From the visitors' point of view, seeing off the first hour and then capitalizing on the day would be ideal. If they bat through the day, they should get somewhere between 300-350, which would, in all means, shut the door for the Afghans.

The track is spinning but it is by no means a minefield. Yes, batting is a bit difficult but given that it is only Day 2, it will not be so difficult. Javed Ahmadi and Ihsanullah showed in the morning session yesterday how to bat while John Campbell and Shamarh Brooks are already playing well. The key is to get oneself set. Once you are in, batting becomes easier. Having said that, it is not a type of pitch where you are always in once set - so concentration and focus are important.

'Bowling, Shane!' Remember this? A certain Adam Gilchrist used to shout behind the stumps when the wizard Shane Warne used to bowl. On Wednesday, there was no use of those two words by Shane Dowrich but boy, Rahkeem Rashawn 'Shane' Cornwall - the man from Antigua, bowled like Shane Warne, albeit off spin, making the Afghan batsmen dance to his turn and bounce as he registered the best ever figures in India in 2019 and also the second best overall this year. His 7/75 derailed what was seeming to look like a train as Afghanistan collapsed from 84/1 to 187 all out. A boring day suddenly became exciting as spin dictated terms. How will Thursday pan out? Hello and a warm welcome to the second day of the one-off Test between Afghanistan and West Indies in Lucknow.

West Indies would have loved to end the day unscathed but that was not the case as the Afghan spinners were all over them and on full fire. The deficit though, is just 119, so one good stand could put Afghanistan under tremendous pressure. So Day 2 promises to be a cracker. With the pitch deteriorating further it will be a challenge for the West Indian batting to resist the likes of Rashid Khan and Amir Hamza. Do join us on Thursday, 28th November, 2019, for Day 2 at 0930 local (0400 GMT). Till then take care, goodbye.

Rahkeem Cornwall says that the strength when he bowls comes from the upper body. Adds that staying balanced and trying to bowl in the right areas are the keys. Feels that the ball is turning and sticking a lot in the surface and if the spinners bowl in the right areas, there is a lot that they can extract from this pitch.

Speaking of the Afghanistan batting, they never looked settled and comfortable against the speedsters or the spinners. Wrong technique and false shots summed up their batting. They were clueless to the spin of Warrican and Cornwall. They collapsed from 84/1 to 111/7. If not for Afsar Zazai and Amir Hamza's fightback, Afghanistan would have failed to reach even 150. Man of the day Rahkeem Cornwall is down for a chat with Alistair Campbell.

All in all an eventful day of Test cricket. 12 wickets fell in a day which belonged to one man, Rahkeem Cornwall. The giant man wreaked havoc in the Afghan camp with his offies. His 7/75 are the best figures in an innings in India, since 2018. Wow. He terrorized even the best in business with his turn and bounce. The day started with Holder winning the toss and putting in the hosts to bat. But soon he was in doubt when there was no assistance to the pacers. Then came the man Rahkeem Cornwall and what he did was remarkable. He generated turn and bounce to trouble the Afghan batsmen. Jason Holder picked up two wickets while Warrican took one.
